raw:
The common room is warmer than the library, the fire reduced to a steady bed of coals. Seraphel is not among the people gathered there.

You take an empty leather chair near the hearth, the blue orientation book resting across your knee.

At the study table, a demon woman with one wrist splinted in pale wood deals cards one-handed. Thessaly stands beside her, watching closely. Two other students occupy the remaining chairs, their discarded cups and a plate of sugared nuts crowded between the score paper and the cards.

The garden door opens. Rashid comes in with his coat over one shoulder, his hair damp at the temples.

He stops at the table. “Dena, I should have sent word. I’m sorry.”

The woman with the splint looks up from her hand. “You should have. Sit down if you mean to play. Don’t turn this into a meeting.”

“Fair.”

Thessaly taps the score paper. “What happens to someone joining late?”

“He takes the lowest score,” Dena says.

“That is sensibly cruel.”

Rashid pulls out the empty chair, accepting the cards Dena pushes toward him. One of the others deals him in without ceremony. The game resumes: cards sliding over wood, Rashid losing the first trick almost immediately, Dena’s brief laugh sharper than the fire’s crackle.

From your chair, you can return to the Council book while the ordinary, competitive business of the room goes on around you.
